content.title: How to watch Timberwolves at Thunder today: game preview, injury updates and TV and streaming info | Minnesota Timberwolves
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves are back in action Sunday with a noon matchup against the Thunder in Oklahoma City.The Wolves are coming off a 127–117 road win over the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Anthony Edwards led the way with 42 points. Rudy Gobert added 18 points and nine rebounds, while Ayo Dosunmu finished with 12 points, eight rebounds and seven assists.Sixth in the West at 41–26, Minnesota is 6–4 over their last 10 and 19–14 on the road. The Wolves rank 11th in defense (113.0 defensive rating) and 12th in offense (116.3 offensive rating).Here’s what to know heading into Sunday’s Wolves–Thunder matinee matchup, including where to watch or stream and the latest injury updates.How to watch, stream & listen to Timberwolves at ThunderDate: Sunday, March 15Start Time: 12 PM CTTV Channel/Live Stream: ABCRadio: iHeartRadio | Timberwolves app Where: Paycom Center | Oklahoma City, OKWolves at Thunder tips off at 12 PM on Sunday, Marhc 15from Paycom Center in Oklahoma City. The game will be broadcast and streamed nationally on ABC.Injury ReportNote: Tonight's injury report will be updated before the start of the game.Timberwolves Out: Julian Philips, Joan Beringer, Enrique Freeman & Zyon PullinJulian Philips (G League On Assignment), Joan Beringer (G League On Assignment), Enrique Freeman (G League Two-Way) and Zyon Pullin (G League Two-Way) are out.ThunderOut: Branden Carlson, Jalen Williams & Thomas SorberBranden Carlson (Low Back Strain), Jalen Williams (Right Hamstring Strain) and Thomas Sorber (Right ACL Surgical Recovery) are out.Jerseys Timberwolves: Icon EditionThunder: Association EditionThe Wolves will be in their blue Icon Edition uniforms against the Thunder, who will be in their white Association Edition uniforms.What to know about the ThunderFirst in the West and owning the NBA’s best record at 52–15, the Thunder enter Sunday on a seven-game win streak and are 9–1 over their last 10. Oklahoma City ranks first in defensive rating (106.3) and seventh in offensive rating (117.0).Sunday marks the fourth and final meeting between the Wolves and Thunder this season. Minnesota leads the series 2–1.Led by All-Stars Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Chet Holmgren, Oklahoma City’s rotation is expected to feature Lu Dort, Cason Wallace, Isaiah Hartenstein, Ajay Mitchell, Jaylin Williams, Aaron Wiggins, Jared McCain, Isaiah Joe and Alex Caruso.
